Title: Select/Move
Content: Select/Move Select/Move Select Deselect Move Select/Move - Select and move 3D garment in the 3D window. - Find the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. - Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move Select - Hover the mouse over the Pattern to be selected in the 3D window. - Click to select the Pattern. - To select multiple Patterns, hold down the Shift key when selecting them. Deselect - To deselect Patterns, click on the 3D window. - To partially deselect, hold down the Shift key and select the Patterns need to be deselected. Move - To move a Pattern, click and drag the desired Pattern.

Title: Binding Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
Content: List of Contents Binding Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Binding Right-Click Pop-Up Menu - Edit Binding using its right-click pop-up menu. - Select the tool from the 3D toolbar. Note: Binding can also be selected with the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. - Right click on the Binding and select desired options as needed. Delete - Delete the selected Binding. Reset Arrangement - Rearrange the Binding patterns to fix unstable simulation. Deactivate/Activate - Activate or deactivate the selected Binding. Freeze/Unfreeze - Freeze or unfreeze the selected Binding.

Title: Add Point or Curve Point to Line (Avatar)
Content: Objective Use the right-click pop-up menu to add point or curve point to modify Lines (Avatar). Location Main Menu 3D Garment Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) 3D Toolbar EEdit 3D Pen (Avatar) When the Avatar is draped in a Garment, the Garment becomes translucent. Right click on the Line (Avatar) where a point or curve point should be added. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Choose Add Point or Add Curve Point as needed. Add Point: a segment point is added to the selected line. Add Curve Point: a curve point is added to the selected line. Select and move the added point or curve point by using the Edit 3D Pen (Avatar) tool to edit 3D Pen (Avatar).

Title: Play Motion
Content: List of Contents Pose Motion Objective Play Pose(*.pos) or Motion(*.mtn) files. Location Main Menu Avatar Play Motion 2D Toolbar Play Motion Operation Pose Open a Pose file. When a Pose file is loaded, the Play Motion tool is automatically activated. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Play Motion 2D Toolbar Play Motion Click the Play Motion tool while the Avatar changes pose. The Avatar stops temporarily. The Avatar changes pose again. Motion Open a Motion file. The Play Motion tool now can be selected. Click the Play Motion tool. The motion is played.

Title: Solidify
Content: List of Contents Solidify Result of Solidify Solidify - Fix the drape of the Pattern and maintain the shape while simulating. - Use the Solidify function when creating a hats cap and a bras cup where Pattern shapes need to be fixed. - Select the Patterns using the Transform Pattern tool, right click, and select the Solidify option from the pop-up menu. - Or, select the Patterns using the Transform Pattern tool, navigate to the Property Editor and toggle on Solidify Result of Solidify - The selected Pattern will maintain its drape. - Set how strong Pattern will maintain its drape by adjusting the Strengthen option. - The Selected Pattern will maintain its drape depending on the Strengthen setting when the Simulation is activated.

Title: Polygon
Content: List of Contents Polygon Create Polygon Create Polygon with Curves Create Polygon with Specific Values Create Points in Guidelines Cancel the Last Action Cancel All Actions Polygon - Create Polygon Patterns in the 2D window. - Select the Polygon tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern Create Polygon. Create Polygon - Select the Polygon tool and click on the 2D window to draw desired shape of Polygon. - Click the start point again to complete the Pattern. Create Polygon with Curves - Hold down the Ctrl key while clicking the 2D window to create curves with the free curve point. - Or, click and drag the mouse while adding a point on the 2D window to create curves with AI Bezier handles. Create Polygon with Specific Values - Click and then right click on the 2D window to access the Create Polygon window. - Type in the desired value to Length. Create Points in Guidelines - Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to add points in a straight line or a diagonal line. Cancel the Last Action - While creating the Polygon Pattern, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action. Cancel All Actions - While creating the Polygon Pattern, hit the Esc or Ctrl+Z keys on the keyboard to cancel all actions.

Title: Add Point to Intersection
Content: Objective Add Segment Points to where segments intersect. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Select the segment that is crossed. The selected segment is highlighted in yellow. Right click on the selected segment. A pop-up menu appears. Select the Add Point to Intersection option. A Segment Point is added to where the segment intersects. Note: The point is only added to the selected segment. To add points to both intersecting segments, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select both segment before right-clicking and selecting Add Point to Intersection option.

Title: [Popup] Mirror Paste Buttonhole
Content: Objective Copy and mirror paste buttonholes (ver2.5.0). Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Buttonhole Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) Click Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click on the copied buttonhole then click Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) from the pop-up menu. Placement preview displays along the mouse in the 2D window. Click on a desired location to paste the buttonholes. Note: Before pasting buttonholes in place, right click to access the Paste window where specific interval and number of buttonholes can be manually input for multiple copy-and-paste. When buttonholes are mirror-pasted, only locations are mirrored whereas other properties, such as Angle, are not.

Title: [Tool] Move Buttonhole
Content: Objective Move buttonholes as desired. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Move Buttonholes with Click-and-Drag Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar Select/Move Button Click and drag the buttonholes to the desired location on either of 2D or 3D Pattern. The selected buttonholes are now being moved accordingly. Note: Move multiple buttonholes at once by selecting them in the 2D window (ver2.4.0). Move Buttonholes with Distance Input (ver2.5.0) Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Window Toolbar Select/Move Button While click-and-dragging the buttonholes with left-click mouse button, click right-click mouse button in either of 2D or 3D window. The Moving Distance window appears. Enter desired value in the menu. Distance Moved Sets the moved distance of the buttonhole from its original location. Position Sets the position of the center of the buttonhole from the left/right/top/bottom of the pattern outline. Click OK. The buttonholes are now being moved according to the input value. Note: Buttonholes can only be moved within the boundaries of the Pattern.

Title: Library Window
Content: Objective Conveniently manage and open files in the program using the Library Window. Add frequently used folders to the Library to easily open files: drag and drop a file from the registered folder into the 3D Window or with the left mouse button, double click the file. Operation Download Download newly added default files as a whole. Selectively download files from the folder with the "N" sign. Reset Reset registered folders in the Library. Add Folder Add frequently used folders to the Library. View the hierarchy of subfolders in the added folder as tree view. Refresh Apply any changes made in the Library such as deleting or adding folders. List / Icon Toggle between different views. Search Use Search to locate files quickly and efficiently within the Library. Note: Hover over the desired Project/Garment file thumbnail to preview font, back, and side views. To change the thumbnail image of a folder in the Library window, please open the corresponding folder installed on your computer. Place the desired image to the folder and rename the image according to below pattern Pattern: CLOicon_FolderName E.g.: CLOicon_Avatar

Title: 3D Pen (Garment)
Content: Objective Draw lines directly on 3D Garments (ver3.0.0). Location 3D Toolbar 3D Pen (Garment) Main Menu 3D Garment 3D Pen (Garment) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar 3D Pen (Garment) Main Menu 3D Garment 3D Pen (Garment) Click a point at desired location of 3D Garments and drag to draw desired 3D lines. Black lines appear and a black dot follows around mouse. Create desired lines or shapes. The created lines or shapes are now being highlighted in yellow color. The created lines or shapes not only appear as Baselines in 3D Garments but also in 2D Patterns. Note: To complete line creation, double-click on the end point. To complete shape creation, the end point should be the same as start point. To create a curved line, press Ctrl button on keyboard while creating the line. When creating a line, its length appears (ver.5.0.0.)

Title: [3D Tool] Edit Tack
Content: List of Contents Edit Tack Delete Tack Objective Edit the position and the spacing of tacks/Avatar or delete unnecessary tacks. Location Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack Operation Edit Tack Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Edit Tack 3D Toolbar Edit Tack The Garment is now being changed to semi-transparent. Click drag on the end point to adjust the position and spacing. Delete Tack Click on a tack to delete. The selected tack is now being highlighted in yellow color. Press 'Delete' on keyboard, or right-click and select Delete among the pop-up menu option. The selected tack is now being deleted.

Title: Express Double Sided
Content: Objective Without putting two Patterns together, it is able to express double sided effect. Location 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern / Transform Pattern Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern / Transform Pattern Select a Pattern or Pattern line to express doubled sided effect. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Property Editor Selected Line Curved Side Geometry Check on Double Sided The selected Pattern or Pattern line is now being displayed as double sided.

Title: Curved Side Geometry
Content: Objective Apply and adjust curvature on edges of Patterns for more natural and realistic look (ver2.2.0). Location 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Operation Firstly, change the 3D Garment rendering style to Thick Textured Surface in the 3D window. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Select a Pattern or Pattern line to express curved sided effect. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Enter a desired value at: Property Editor Selected Line Curved Side Geometry Curvature (%) The curvature is now being applied according to the entered value. Note: The maximum Curvature (%) value is 50 percent (%) of the fabric thickness. For instance, if the fabric thickness is being set at 1mm, the maximum Curvature (%) is 0.5mm.

Title: CLO Garment Fit Maps Guide
Content: Download our guide to garment fit maps. GARMENT FIT MAPS Overview Stress Map Fit Map Garment Fit Properties WORKFLOW Checklist Example Workflow How to Export Garment Fit Maps

Title: Bill of Material
Content: Objective Estimate cost per the number and price of fabric, buttons, and buttonholes. Location Main Menu Editor BOM Operation Select the indicated menu. The mode is converted to BOM. Select the colorway to estimate the cost. Fabric, button, buttonholes, topstitch, and zipper(ver 7.2) of the selected colorway appear. Assign units to each item and input cost per item. The cost is calculated based on the input values. The cost of all colorways shows on the top of the BOM Editor. Note: As the estimated cost of fabric is calculated based on the Print Layout's fabric consumption, it is recommended to place Patterns in the Print Layout Mode first. Click the Update button on the right top corner of the BOM Editor after changing fabric and trims.

Title: Topstitch Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
Content: Topstitch Right-Click Pop-Up Menu - Right click on the Topstitch to access the right-click pop-up menu. - Select Edit Topstitch tool from the 2D toolbar. - Right click on the Topstitch and select the desired option from the right-click pop-up menu. Select All With Same Property Select all Topstitches that have the same property with clicked Topstitch. Assign to New Topstitch Apply a new Topstitch style to selected Topstitch. A new Topstitch style is added and applied to selected Topstitch. Delete Delete selected Topstitch. D. Add Internal Line on Topstitch _ver4.2.0 An Internal Line is created on top of selected Topstitch.

Title: Transform OBJ Trims
Content: List of Contents Via the Scale Gizmo Via the Property Editor Objective Transform OBJ files loaded as trim as needed. Location Via the Scale Gizmo Load OBJ as Trim Scale Via the Property Editor Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Via the Scale Gizmo Load an OBJ. Follow the indicated guideline below: Load OBJ as Trim Scale The Scale Gizmo appears. Click and drag on the x,y, or z-axis to transform the OBJ. Axis Description X-Axis The red axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the x-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its x-axis. Y-Axis The yellow-green axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the y-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its y-axis. Z-Axis The blue axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the z-axis to transform the OBJ along its z-axis. Square The yellow square located in the center of the Scale Gizmo. Click and drag the square to transform the OBJ trim, while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. The OBJ is transformed. When the OBJ transformation is complete, click the Scale button again. The Gizmo used for moving and rotating OBJs appears. Via the Property Editor Load an OBJ. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select the OBJ to be transformed. The properties of the OBJ appear in the Property Editor. Find the Scale option. Enter the desired value for below options. Option Description X-Axis Enter the desired x-axis value. Y-Axis Enter the desired y-axis value. Z-Axis Enter the desired z-axis value. Maintain Ratio Toggle this option on to adjust an OBJ while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio.

Title: Basic Circumference Measurement
Content: List of Contents Basic Circumference Measurement Measure Circumference Basic Circumference Measurement - Measure a circumference of an Avatar. - Select the Basic Circumference Measurement tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate to Main Menu Avatar Measurement Basic Circumference Measurement. Measure Circumference - Select the Basic Circumference Measurement tool from the 3D Toolbar. - Left click the total of three times to measure the Avatars circumference. - Click once to start the Circumference Measurement, then move the mouse and click again to assign the measurement direction. - Hover the mouse over the purple line connecting the first and the second point and move the mouse to assign the circumference angle. - When the desired circumference angle is achieved, left click to complete the Circumference Measurement. - After establishing the first point of the circumference, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create the second and third point in a straight line.

Title: Strengthen
Content: List of Contents Strengthen Result of Strengthen Strengthen - Temporarily harden Patterns while simulating the 3D Garment. - Strengthen when folding or straightening Patterns in the 3D window. - Use the Transform Pattern tool to select patterns, right click, and select Strengthen. Windows Shortcut: Ctrl + H Mac Shortcut: Ctrl + L (ver5.0.0) Result of Strengthen - When the Patterns are strengthened properly, they turn orange. - The Patterns will temporarily gain strength and express clean folds where fold angles are applied. - To unstrengthen the Pattern, use the Transform Pattern tool to select Pattern, right click, and select Unstrengthen. Windows Shortcut: Ctrl + H Mac Shortcut: Ctrl + L (ver5.0.0)

Title: Zipper Slider/Stopper Properties
Content: Objective Set the Zipper Slider and Stopper properties. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Select the tool/menu indicated. Select a Zipper or Stopper created on a 3D Garment and modify its properties: Option Description Open/Save (ver 7.2 ) Save the properties of the slider(ZSL), puller(ZPU), and stopper(ZST) as each file. Name Name the zipper. Shape Set the zipper to be one-way or two-way. (ver 2024.0) Note: For two-way zippers, you can set the locking direction to either head-to-head or Bottom-to-Bottom. Changing the slider material will be applied identically to both sides. Slider Select a shape for the slider. Note: When applying All-in-one preset for the Slider &amp Puller, the puller cannot be disabled and changed. Puller Select a shape for the puller. Stopper Select the Stopper type (Open / Closed End) and then select shapes for Top and Bottom. A selection of Bottom shapes is configured based on the shape of the Stopper. Specification Gauge Select the size of the Slider by Gauge(#) or percentage. Weight (g) Assign the weight of the slider. Fasten Zipper Reverse Zip Direction Select the zip direction. The slider is relocated based on the option. Move to Opposite Side Select a side of the zipper tape where the slider will locate when the zipper is open. Material Set the Material Type and Texture of the selected object.(ver 7.1) - Select All: If you select one of the Slider/Puller/Stopper, it will be selected at once. - Select Object: If you click the object to be selected once more in the state of selecting all objects, only the object is selected. - Select part of an object: If the object is divided into two or more meshes, click once more with the object selected to select only that part.

Title: Video Capture 3D Garment (Turntable)
Content: List of Contents Record Quit Objective Easily record 3D garments with Turntable, utilize it when communicating. Location Record Main Menu File Video Capture Turntable Quit X button on the top-right corner of Turntable dialogue X Button Operation Record Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Turntable dialogue window appears at the bottom-right corner. Set options as needed and start recording. Video Size Adjust the orientation, width and height of the turntable video window. Options Rotation Axis (ver 6.1) Set the rotation axis of a Turntable video. Auto The axis is set to the center of the garment and avatar in the 3D window. Center (0.0) The axis is set to the center (0.0) in the 3D window. Custom Enter the desired value of the X and Z-axis to set the desired axis. Direction Set the direction (clockwise/ counter-clockwise) of the turntable. Duration Set the duration of the turntable video. Minimum of 1 second and a maximum of 60 seconds. Save HTML File The turntable is saved as HTML. Video Codec Set the codec to use when recording video. Note: it is available to save MP4/AVI for Windows and MOV files for MAC without installing a separate codec. Record / Start or delete the recording and return to the initial state. Quit Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Recording stops and the dialogue window disappears.

Title: OBJ Sequence Export
Content: Objective Export an OBJ Sequence as an OBJ file on every frame of an animation. Exporting a 1 second animation with a 30 fps standard will result in 30 OBJ files being exported. Location Main Menu File Export Animation OBJ Sequence Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Export Animation OBJ Sequence The Save File window opens. Select the desired file and click OK. The Export OBJ Animation window opens. Set below options as needed and click OK. Export OBJ Animation Option Object Select All Patterns: Select/Deselect all patterns. You can select specific patterns by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). When utilizing the OBJ (Selected) menu, patterns selected in the 3D and 2D windows are automatically selected and checkbox-ed. Select All Avatars: Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. You can select specific objects by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Select All Graphics and Trims: Select/Deselect all Graphics and Trims. You can select specific stitches by utilizing the dropdown menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Single Object Exports the selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects Exports the selected object as multiple objects. UnWeld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0. (ver2.3.0). Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Combined UV Coordinates Include Internal Shape: Include internal line and/or shape information in export (ver2.3.0). Scale Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from Unit in file to import is selected. Axis Conversion Changes the directions of each axis of the object. Animation Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.) Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.)

Title: [2D Tool] M:N Free Sewing
Content: Objective Freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns (M) to multiple Patterns (N) at once. Location Main Menu Sewing M:N Free Sewing 2D Toolbar M:N Free Sewing Note: Hold down the Free Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Free Sewing Tool. Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing M:N Free Sewing 2D Toolbar M:N Free Sewing Establish Free Sewing Lines on multiple Patterns, which are considered as M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. While being mindful of Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on Patterns which are sewn to M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M:N Sewing Lines. All Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. Note: While establishing the Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. While establishing M:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied.

Title: [Property] Create 2D Buttonhole Measurement
Content: Objective View buttonhole position from the pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). Location Object Browser Buttonhole Property Editor 2D Measurements To Center Operation Select a buttonhole with Select/Move Button tool in the 3D toolbar. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Property Editor 2D Measurements To Center Select the desired 2D measurement options of the Left/Right/Up/Down. The 2D measurement is now being displayed or hidden accordingly.

Title: [Popup] Delete Sewing
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary Sewing Lines. Location 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Tool Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Delete Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Edit Sewing Tool Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Sewing Line) Delete Sewing Note: You can also delete the Sewing Line by select hit the Delete key on the keyboard.

Title: Change Length
Content: Objective Type in the segment length and edit Pattern. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location Right-click on the segment to be adjusted to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Change Length. The Change Length window appears. Set each option and click the OK button. Length Enter the length of the segment to change. Direction Set the direction to change the length. Lock Curve Points If a line connected to the selected line is a curve, the curve point is moved according to the changed length. To move only straight point, click this option. The segment length is changed accordingly. Note: When clicking continuous line segements, it is recognized as a single segment and change in length (ver 7.1)

Title: Merge Points on Internal Lines
Content: List of Contents Join Overlapping Points Merge to Point Merge to Average Intersect &amp Merge Objective Join or merge two open points on Internal Lines. Note: When a point on the Internal Line is open, it is hollow, whereas when a point on the Internal Line is closed, it is filled. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Operation Join Overlapping Points Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Select overlapping points and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Join Overlapping Points. Two overlapping points are joined and closed. Merge to Point Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Select two points on Internal Lines to be merged. Right click on the point which the other point should be merged to. When the pop-up menu appears, select Merge to Point. The point is merged to the right-clicked point. Merge to Average Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Select two points on the Internal Lines to be merged. Then, right click on either point to access the pop-up menu and select Merge to Average. The selected points are merged to their average point. Intersect &amp Merge Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Select two points to be merged. Right click on the points to access the pop-up menu and select Intersect &amp Merge. The selected points are shortened or extended maintaining their current slope and are merged where they intersect.

Title: 3D Window
Content: Objective 3D Window is a 3D area where it is possible to simulate garments and move avatars to create animations. Starting from ver 5.2, high-quality render is offered in the 3D window. Note: It is recommended to turn On/Off the Quality Render option as needed since it is slower than the regular render. Location Show/ Hide 3D Window Main Menu Display Windows 3D Garment Window Quality Render (3D Window) Main Menu Render Quality Render (3D Window) Icon in the 3D Window Quality Render (3D Window) Operation Select the menu/tool indicated in Location. The render quality of the 3D Window is improved.

Title: Clone as Pattern/Internal Shape
Content: List of Contents Clone as Pattern Clone as Pattern (with Sewing) Objective Duplicate an Internal Shape as an identical shaped Pattern or vice-versa. Operation Clone as Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern (A) Right click on the Internal Shape to be duplicated as a Pattern to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Clone as Pattern. The duplicated Pattern follows along the mouse cursor. Click on the 2D window to place the Pattern. Clone as Pattern (with Sewing) (ver 7.3) Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern (Z) Click the Pattern to be duplicated and the connecting segment to be automatically sewn. Then, right-click click the Clone as Pattern (with Sewing). It is duplicated in a pattern connecting the start/end points of the selected segment. The duplicated pattern follows along the mouse cursor. Click on the desired Pattern to place the Internal Shape. It is duplicated with the selected internal line automatically sewn. Note: When the internal shape is selected and clone as a pattern (with Sewing), the entire pattern is sewn.
